chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Is the Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar) during the Days of Tashreeq after the prayers?' He said: 'The Takbir is in Mina after fifteen prayers, and in the other regions after ten prayers. The first Takbir is after the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Nahr (Sacrifice), saying: Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, La ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, for what Allah has guided us to, Allahu Akbar, for what He has provided us from the beasts of grazing livestock. And the Takbir was made to be after ten prayers in the other regions because when the people depart in the first departure, the people of the regions refrain from the Takbir, and the people of Mina continue to say Takbir as long as they are in Mina until the final departure.'

key_terms.بَهِيمَةُ الْأَنْعَامِ: Beasts of grazing livestock (camels, cattle, sheep, goats)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct number of prayers after which Takbir is recited during the Days of Tashreeq in Mina versus other regions?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* details the specific protocol for Takbir al-Tashriq, distinguishing between the extended recitation in Mina (after fifteen prayers) and the abbreviated form in other regions (after ten prayers). It highlights the scholarly understanding that the delay in other regions prevents confusion with the pilgrims in Mina, ensuring the communal glorification remains synchronized with the Hajj rituals. The text also provides the exact liturgical formula, emphasizing gratitude for divine guidance and sustenance.
